To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TIP, a thyroid hormone-induced protein, is a transcriptional product of T(3).
thyroid hormone (T(3)), through its receptor, induces a 52-kD protein (TIP), which modulates Delta(5)- 3beta-HSD, a key enzyme in progesterone formation.
T(3) induces the generation of a protein (TIP), which, in turn, increases Delta(5)-Delta (4)-isomerase activity by a mechanism involving protein-protein interaction between TIP and Delta(5)3betaHSD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
thyroid hormone regulation of ovarian function in the perch.
the thyroid hormone-induced protein (52 kDa), which is a novel regulatory protein of the ovarian follicle.
the identification of a novel TIP protein in the ovarian follicles of perch and its role in the regulation of steroidogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T(3) induction of TIP in the perch ovarian theca cells is a primary event and the TIP induction of Delta(5) 3beta-HSD is a secondary event.
the thyroid hormone-induced protein (52 kDa), which has been found in the perch ovarian theca cells, is a protein that is induced by thyroid hormone and not by gonadotropins.

thyroid hormone (T(3)), through the generation of a TIP (52-kDa protein), stimulates Delta(5)- 3beta-HSD in the perch ovarian tissue by modulating its activity, and thus increases progesterone secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

thyroid hormone regulates the reproductive function in perch by inducing the synthesis of TIP protein, which in turn activates Delta(5)-Delta4-isomerase activity of the 3beta-hydroxy steroid dehydrogenase enzyme.

thyroid hormone (T(3)), through the induction of TIP in the ovarian follicles of perch, modulates the activity of Delta(5-3beta-HSD by protein-protein interaction, which, in turn, regulates the progesterone biosynthesis.
T(3) induces TIP, which in turn activates the Delta(5)-Delta4-isomerase (3beta-HSD) enzyme by a protein-protein mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TIP is the thyroid hormone receptor protein which regulates the Delta(5)-Delta4-steroid conversion enzyme activity in the ovarian follicles of perch.
T(3) induces the generation of TIP protein, which in turn activates Delta(5)- 3beta-HSD, the key enzyme for progesterone synthesis, by a mechanism involving protein-protein interaction.

thyroid hormone (3,5, 3'-triiodo-L-thyronine (T3)) stimulates the expression of a 52 kDa monomer protein (TIP, thyroid hormone-induced protein) which in turn increases the Delta(5)- 3beta-hydroxy steroid dehydrogenase activity (3beta-HSD) of the ovarian follicle.
